title: In A Grove

speaker_display.monk: the traveling monk who met the couple the day before
speaker_display.narrator: the outside narrator who only introduces who is speaking
speaker_display.woodcutter: the woodcutter who found the body

items.speaker_state: He is matter-of-factly reporting what he saw. No emotion or manner is stated.
items.scene: He reports seeing a stab wound in the chest.
evidence: "One stab in the chest. That's what I saw,"

items.speaker_state: He is giving a factual account of finding the body and the signs at the scene. No emotion or manner is stated.
items.scene: He tells the listener what he found that morning in a thicket off the mountain road.
items.reaction_to_previous: He adds details to his earlier report of the chest wound.
evidence: "One stab in the chest. That's what I saw,"
"The broken bamboo and trampled earth showed a struggle."

items.speaker_state: He is simply stating when he passed the couple; no emotion or manner is stated.
items.scene: He says he passed the couple the previous day at noon.
items.reaction_to_previous: He adds his account after the woodcutter describes finding the body and the scene.

items.speaker_state: He regrets not having paid closer attention to the couple. No other feeling is stated.
items.scene: He recalls seeing the couple and says he wishes he had looked at them more carefully.
items.reaction_to_previous: He expands on when he passed the couple, adding what he saw and his regret.
evidence: "I hardly looked at them. Now I wish I had."

items.speaker_state: He is reporting that he caught the bandit; no emotion or manner is stated.
items.scene: He tells the listener he caught Tajomaru by the stone bridge.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows the monk's account with news that the bandit was caught.
evidence: "I caught Tajomaru, the famous bandit, by the stone bridge,"

items.speaker_state: He gives practical instructions about finding the woman. No emotion or manner is stated.
items.scene: After reporting the capture, he describes the man's fall and bow, then directs someone to find the woman.
items.reaction_to_previous: He adds details about the captured man and tells the listener what to do next.
evidence: "He'd fallen from a horse, but he still had the dead man's bow."

items.speaker_state: She identifies Takehiro as her daughter's husband. No emotion or manner is stated in this line.
items.scene: She tells the listener who Takehiro was in relation to her daughter.
items.reaction_to_previous: She responds to the constable's instruction to find the woman by identifying Takehiro as her daughter's husband.

items.speaker_state: She is pleading for help and news about Masago, with concern for her daughter evident.
items.scene: She asks that Masago be found and that she not be sent home without news.
items.reaction_to_previous: She follows her identification of Takehiro with a plea to find her daughter.
evidence: "Masago is proud, yes, but she's only nineteen."

items.speaker_state: He acknowledges that he killed the man. No emotion or manner is stated in this line.
items.scene: He answers the account of the dead man's family by admitting the killing.
items.reaction_to_previous: He responds to the old woman's plea with an admission that he killed the man.

items.speaker_state: He is defensive, insisting that the listener hear his account before judging him. He recounts events with confidence about the fight.
items.scene: He gives his account of the attack, the couple's actions, the fight, and his departure from the thicket.
items.reaction_to_previous: He elaborates on his admission and urges the listener not to call him a coward.
evidence: "But listen before you call me a coward!"
"Twenty-three strokes! No other man had lasted twenty."

items.speaker_state: She describes what she did after the bandit left. No emotion or manner is stated in this brief line.
items.scene: At the temple, she says she crawled towards her husband after the bandit left.
items.reaction_to_previous: She begins her account of what happened after the bandit's version of the events.
evidence: "I crawled towards my husband after the bandit left,"

items.speaker_state: She is distressed and regretful as she recounts stabbing her husband and says she has nowhere to go.
items.scene: At the temple, she describes finding her husband, stabbing him, and trying to drown herself afterward.
items.reaction_to_previous: She continues her account, describing what happened when she reached her husband and what followed.
evidence: "I begged him to die with me."

items.speaker_state: He begins recounting what he heard after Masago crawled towards him; no emotion or manner is stated in this line.
items.scene: Speaking through the medium, he says he heard the bandit comforting Masago.
items.reaction_to_previous: He begins a different account of the moments after Masago reached him.

items.speaker_state: He recounts betrayal, his own death, and the unseen hand taking the dagger. No specific feeling is stated.
items.scene: Speaking through the medium, he describes his wife's words, his death in the thicket, and sinking into darkness.
items.reaction_to_previous: He continues his account, explaining what happened after he heard the bandit comforting Masago.
evidence: "I sank for ever into the darkness."
